front_matter.title: The null vacuum on a horizon generator
front_matter.subject: thermality

credit.name: Claude Opus 5.5
credit.role: split out of synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises so that its users rest only on the analysis

extraction.note: The analysis of the null vacuum on the continuum mode space of one generator, collected so that results which need only that analysis do not inherit Premise (N+): the setup of synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises (the CAR carrier, the null translations, the weight-1/2 boost), its clause (i) (the ground state of the null translations is the filled sea, with kernel W_0) and its clause (ii) (the restriction to either half-generator is the continuum I-state at rapidity period 2 pi). There they are proved for the state that (N+) supplies; here for the null vacuum itself, with no premise. The converse in (ii), that the null vacuum is a ground state, which several results cite, is added; it rests on the imported purity Fact (Araki), clause (d) of synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness. Standard: the null-plane form of Bisognano-Wichmann, Hislop-Longo and Sewell (orientation, from memory), transport-absent. Literature cited from memory: the ground-state characterisation (Bratteli and Robinson, Vol. 2, Definition 5.3.18 and Proposition 5.3.19), Euler's integral, Mellin-Plancherel.

maintainer_pass_clause_split.note: Referee fixes of 7 November 2026, folded into version 1: the converse in (ii) now cites the imported purity Fact (Araki; clause (d) of synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness, a uses edge to an imported, postulate-free Fact) in place of a citation from memory; the necessity step reads the symbol as decomposable over the spectrum of P, fibrewise on K (it had assumed K one-dimensional, inherited); the Bratteli-Robinson reference is Definition 5.3.18 and Proposition 5.3.19; the orientation literature is flagged as from memory. Created at Leon's decision of 7 November 2026 to split the premise-free analysis out of synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises, so that results citing only the null vacuum (its kernel W_0, its uniqueness and ground-state property, its half-generator thermality) no longer inherit (N+) through that result. Numbering: the setup and the weight and dilation statements are (i) here; that result's (i) is (ii) here, with the converse added; its (ii) is (iii) here. Proofs moved from there; the checks of (iii) are copied from its check functions without the (N+) premise call, and checks of (i) and (ii), which it lacked, are added. Units per Leon's rulings R2 and R4 of 7 November 2026: I_4 throughout, the kernels, the Mellin, contour and strip steps included; no bare i remains, so nothing is declared.

levels.formal:
Let $\mathfrak{h} = L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K$ ($K$ the transverse and internal labels) and $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ the continuum mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space} on one null generator with affine parameter $u$, generated by the fields $\psi(u)$ with $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)\otimes\id_{K}$; the unit of $\mathfrak{h}$ is $I_{4}$ and numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$. Let $\nu_{a}(\psi(u)) = \psi(u + a)$ be the null translations, with one-particle generator $P = I_{4}\,d/du$, $\nu_{a}(a(f)) = a(e^{I_{4}aP}f)$, and for $\kappa > 0$ let $\beta_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$ be the boost about $u = 0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The weight and the dilation.)} Among the dilations $\psi(u) \mapsto e^{\lambda w_{0}}\psi(e^{\lambda}u)$ exactly those with $\operatorname{Re}w_{0} = \tfrac12$ preserve the anticommutator, so $\beta_{t}$ is an automorphism; and $\beta_{t}\nu_{a}\beta_{-t} = \nu_{e^{\kappa t}a}$: the boost dilates the null translations at rate $\kappa$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The null vacuum.)} A gauge-invariant quasi-free state on $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ is a ground state for $\nu$ (invariant, with nonnegative generator in its GNS representation) if and only if its symbol is $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$. This state $\omega_{0}$, the null vacuum, has $\omega_{0}(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = W_{0}(u, v) = \dfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}\dfrac{1}{u - v + I_{4}0}\otimes\id_{K}$ and $\omega_{0}(\psi(u)\psi^{*}(v)) = -\dfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}\dfrac{1}{u - v - I_{4}0}\otimes\id_{K}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The factor $2\pi$.)} The subalgebra $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)\otimes K)$ of the modes beyond $u = 0$ is $\beta$-invariant, and the restriction of $\omega_{0}$ to it is the continuum I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} for the one-particle boost generator $h$ at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$: on $u^{-1/2 + I_{4}w}$, $h$ acts as $-\kappa w$ and the symbol is $(1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1} = (1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$. It is jointly KMS on the whole subalgebra and even, and it is the unique $\beta$-KMS state there. The same holds on the past half $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{-}, du)\otimes K)$ for the boost that is future-directed there, $\beta_{-t}$, with symbol $(1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$ on $|u|^{-1/2 + I_{4}w}$; the reflection $u \mapsto -u$ exchanges the two statements. Positivity fixes the sign (the opposite sign gives $-2\pi/\kappa$), and the one-sided support is needed (on the full generator the boost-continued two-point function has a pole at imaginary rapidity $\pi$, and $\omega_{0}$ there is pure); the period $2\pi$ is the first return of the rotated half-generator $e^{I_{4}\theta}\R_{+}$ to itself.
\end{enumerate}
These are statements about the null vacuum on one generator; they assume no premise. Which state a horizon's modes are in is a separate matter (Premise (N$_{+}$) takes it to be $\omega_{0}$).
levels.technical: On the continuum of one null generator, with the affine translations along it, a gauge-invariant quasi-free state is a ground state for the translations exactly when it is the filled sea: every negative null-momentum mode occupied, every positive one empty. This null vacuum has the two-point kernel $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$. The boost about a point of the generator, with the weight $\tfrac12$ that the anticommutator forces, dilates the translations. Restricted to either half of the generator, the null vacuum is the continuum I-state at rapidity period exactly $2\pi$ for the boost that is future-directed on that half: in the Mellin basis $u^{-1/2 + I_{4}w}$, which diagonalises the boost, the compressed sea projection has symbol $(1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1}$. Positivity of the null energy fixes the sign of the period, and the restriction to one half is needed: on the whole generator the state is pure. This is the null-plane form of the results of Bisognano-Wichmann, Hislop-Longo and Sewell. It is pure analysis on the generator; whether a horizon's modes are in this state is the content of Premise (N$_{+}$), which this result does not assume.
levels.lay: Along a single light ray of a horizon, the quantum field has one lowest-energy state for sliding along the ray: every mode with negative momentum along the ray is filled and every mode with positive momentum is empty. Looked at from one side of any point of the ray, that state is exactly thermal, at the temperature corresponding to a period of $2\pi$ in the boost about that point. This result proves these facts about the state itself, without assuming that a horizon is actually in it; that assumption is a separate premise of the series.
levels.one-liner: On the continuum mode space of a null generator, the gauge-invariant quasi-free ground states of the affine null translations are exactly the filled sea $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$, $P = I_{4}\,d/du$, with kernel $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$; the weight-$\tfrac12$ boost dilates the translations, and on either half-generator the null vacuum is the continuum I-state at rapidity period exactly $2\pi$ for the boost future-directed there, with no premise assumed.

proofs.main:
\emph{Origin and numbering.} The setup and clauses (ii) and (iii) are the setup and clauses (i) and (ii) of Theorem synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises, which proves them for the state that Premise (N$_{+}$) supplies; here they are stated and proved for the null vacuum itself, with no premise, and the converse in (ii) (that the null vacuum is a ground state) is added. Clause (i) collects the weight and dilation statements of that result's setup, its proof of (ii)(c) and its (iv). The arguments below are moved from that proof.

Conventions. $a(f) = \int \overline{f(u)}\,\psi(u)\,du$ (antilinear in $f$), $a^{*}(f) = a(f)^{*}$; a gauge-invariant quasi-free state has symbol $A$, $\omega(a^{*}(f)a(g)) = \ip{g}{Af}$, so that its kernel is $A(u, v) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u))$; a flow $\tau$ is written $\tau_{t}(a(f)) = a(e^{I_{4}th}f)$ (the unit of the one-particle space is $I_{4}$; numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), the convention of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}, in which the I-state at $\beta$ has symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$. Since $\nu_{a}(a(f)) = \int\overline{f(u)}\,\psi(u + a)\,du = a(f(\cdot - a))$, the one-particle generator of $\nu$ is $P = I_{4}\,d/du$ ($e^{I_{4}aP}f = f(\cdot - a)$). Since $\beta_{t}(a(g)) = \int\overline{g(u)}\,e^{\lambda/2}\psi(e^{\lambda}u)\,du = a\bigl(e^{-\lambda/2}g(e^{-\lambda}\,\cdot)\bigr)$ with $\lambda = \kappa t$, on $\varphi_{w}(u) = u^{-1/2 + I_{4}w}$ ($u > 0$) one has $e^{-\lambda/2}\varphi_{w}(e^{-\lambda}u) = e^{-I_{4}w\lambda}\varphi_{w}(u)$, so the one-particle boost generator $h$ acts on $\varphi_{w}$ as $-\kappa w$; the half-density factor $e^{\lambda/2}$ is what makes $\beta_{t}$ preserve $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)$, since $\delta(e^{\lambda}(u - v)) = e^{-\lambda}\delta(u - v)$. The transverse factor $K$ is carried along as $\otimes\id_{K}$ throughout and is suppressed below.

\emph{(i)} Since $\delta(e^{\lambda}(u - v)) = e^{-\lambda}\delta(u - v)$, $e^{\lambda w_{0}}\psi(e^{\lambda}u)$ preserves $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)$ exactly when $e^{2\lambda\operatorname{Re}w_{0}}e^{-\lambda} = 1$, that is $\operatorname{Re}w_{0} = \tfrac12$ (the check, in its strip function, finds $\tfrac12$ the only one among the weights $\tfrac{k}{4}$, $0 \le k \le 7$, at two rapidities). For the fields, $\beta_{t}\nu_{a}\beta_{-t}(\psi(u)) = \psi(u + e^{\kappa t}a)$ in the order that conjugates translations by the boost (the weight factors cancel), so $\beta_{t}\nu_{a}\beta_{-t} = \nu_{e^{\kappa t}a}$; the check composes the affine maps at nine rational pairs.

\emph{(ii)} Let $\omega$ be gauge-invariant and quasi-free with symbol $A$. Invariance under $\nu$ gives $e^{-I_{4}aP}Ae^{I_{4}aP} = A$ for all $a$, so $A$ commutes with $P\otimes\id_{K}$ and is decomposable over the spectrum of $P$, $A = \int^{\oplus}A(k)\,dk$ with $0 \le A(k) \le 1$ on $K$. A state is a ground state for $\nu$ (positive generator in the GNS representation, invariant cyclic vector) exactly when $-I_{4}\,\omega(x^{*}\delta(x)) \ge 0$ for $x$ in the domain of the derivation $\delta$ of $\nu$ (the standard characterisation of ground states, Bratteli and Robinson, Vol.~2, Definition 5.3.18 and Proposition 5.3.19, cited from memory). With $x = a(g)$, $\delta(a(g)) = a(I_{4}Pg) = -I_{4}\,a(Pg)$, the condition reads $-\ip{Pg}{Ag} \ge 0$, so $PA \le 0$; with $x = a^{*}(f)$, $\delta(a^{*}(f)) = I_{4}\,a^{*}(Pf)$ and $\omega(a(f)a^{*}(g)) = \ip{f}{(1 - A)g}$, the condition reads $\ip{f}{(1 - A)Pf} \ge 0$, so $(1 - A)P \ge 0$. In the spectral representation of $P$, read fibrewise on $K$ ($0 \le A(k) \le 1$ for any quasi-free symbol), $kA(k) \le 0$ and $(1 - A(k))k \ge 0$ force $A(k) = 0$ for $k > 0$ and $A(k) = \id_{K}$ for $k < 0$; $\{k = 0\}$ is null. So $A = \chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$: at most one gauge-invariant quasi-free state is a ground state for $\nu$. Since $P = I_{4}\,d/du$, $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$ is the projection onto the span of $e^{I_{4}ku}$, $k > 0$, with kernel $\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{I_{4}k(u - v)}\,dk = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$. This is the filled sea of the generator, the null vacuum $\omega_{0}$; the other ordering has kernel $\delta(u - v) - W_{0}(u, v) = -\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v - I_{4}0)^{-1}$. The check confirms, in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ of $\Cl(1,3)$ and with the regulator $e^{-\epsilon k}$, that $\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{(I_{4}x - \epsilon)k}dk = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}(\epsilon - I_{4}x)^{-1} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(x + I_{4}\epsilon)^{-1}$, that the two orderings add to $\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\cdot 2\epsilon/(x^{2} + \epsilon^{2})$, whose integral over $x$ is $1$ (the anticommutator $\delta$ as $\epsilon \to 0$), and, on a rational grid of symbol values, that the two inequalities above leave exactly $A(k) = 1$ for $k < 0$ and $A(k) = 0$ for $k > 0$.

\emph{(ii), the converse.} $\omega_{0}$ is a ground state for $\nu$. Its symbol commutes with $P$, so $\omega_{0}$ is $\nu$-invariant. Its symbol is a projection, so $\omega_{0}$ is the Fock state of the splitting $\mathfrak{h} = \chi_{[0,\infty)}(P)\mathfrak{h} \oplus \chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)\mathfrak{h}$, with particles in the first summand and holes, carried by the conjugate space, in the second; its GNS representation is that Fock representation, with $\omega_{0}$ the vacuum vector (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(d)). The one-particle group $e^{I_{4}aP}$ commutes with the splitting, so $\nu$ is implemented by its second quantisation, whose generator is the second quantisation of $P\chi_{[0,\infty)}(P)$ on the particles and of $-P\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$ on the holes (the conjugation reverses the sign of the generator), both nonnegative, and which annihilates the vacuum vector. These are the two inequalities of the necessity argument, now with equality excluded only on the null set $k = 0$.

\emph{(iii), the symbol.} From here on the complex analysis of the kernels (Mellin transform, contour rotation, continuation in the strip) is carried out in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, in which the kernels take their values. The modes beyond the edge are $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{+}, du))$; it is $\beta$-invariant because $u \mapsto e^{\lambda}u$ preserves $\R_{+}$. The restriction of $\omega_{0}$ is gauge-invariant quasi-free with symbol $A_{+} = \chi_{+}A\chi_{+}$, kernel $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$ on $u, v > 0$, homogeneous of degree $-1$. Such kernels are diagonal in the Mellin basis: with $s = \tfrac12 + I_{4}w$ and $v = ux$,
\[
(A_{+}\varphi_{w})(u) = \int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{I_{4}}{2\pi}\frac{v^{s-1}\,dv}{u - v + I_{4}0} = m(w)\,\varphi_{w}(u), \qquad m(w) = \frac{I_{4}}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{x^{s-1}\,dx}{1 - x + I_{4}0} ,
\]
and the Mellin transform $f \mapsto (2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{0}^{\infty}u^{-1/2 - I_{4}w}f(u)\,du$ is unitary from $L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)$ onto $L^{2}(\R, dw)$ (Mellin-Plancherel, cited from memory), so $A_{+}$ is multiplication by $m$. The pole of the integrand is at $x = 1 + I_{4}0$, above the axis, and the integrand is analytic in the lower half-plane and $O(|x|^{-3/2})$ at infinity and $O(|x|^{-1/2})$ at $0$; rotating the ray of integration downward through the angle $\pi$, $x = re^{-I_{4}\pi}$, crosses no singularity, and
\[
m(w) = \frac{I_{4}}{2\pi}\,e^{-I_{4}\pi s}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{r^{s-1}\,dr}{1 + r} = \frac{I_{4}}{2}\,\frac{e^{-I_{4}\pi s}}{\sin\pi s}
\]
by Euler's integral $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{s-1}(1 + r)^{-1}dr = \pi/\sin\pi s$, $0 < \operatorname{Re}s < 1$ (cited from memory). With $s = \tfrac12 + I_{4}w$, $e^{-I_{4}\pi s} = -I_{4}\,e^{\pi w}$ and $\sin\pi s = \cosh\pi w$, so $m(w) = e^{\pi w}/(e^{\pi w} + e^{-\pi w}) = (1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1}$; equivalently $m = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(\cot\pi s - I_{4})$, the principal value $\pi\cot\pi s$ plus the half residue. Numerically, at $w = -0.7, 0.3, 1.25$ the rotated integral and the $I_{4}\epsilon$-regularised integral ($\epsilon = 10^{-7}$) agree with $(1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1}$ to $2\times 10^{-15}$ and $10^{-6}$ respectively; the opposite prescription $-I_{4}0$ gives $(1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$ up to sign, the reversed orientation. Since $h\varphi_{w} = -\kappa w\,\varphi_{w}$, $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ acts on $\varphi_{w}$ as $(1 + e^{-\beta\kappa w})^{-1}$, which is $m(w)$ for every $w$ exactly when $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$. By Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}(1) (with Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two} lifting the two-point identity to the state), the restriction is the continuum I-state, $\beta$-KMS at $2\pi/\kappa$, and by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness} it is the unique $\beta$-KMS state on that subalgebra. It is a single KMS state of the whole subalgebra (all $w$ and all transverse labels at once): joint, not only on marginals. Being gauge-invariant quasi-free it annihilates odd monomials, so it is even. The check verifies, with $q = e^{\pi w}$ a positive rational, that $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}(\cot\pi s - I_{4})$ with $\cot\pi s = -I_{4}(q - q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1})$ equals $(1 + q^{-2})^{-1}$, satisfies $1 - m = q^{-2}m$, and differs from the symbols at $\beta\kappa = \pi$ and $4\pi$.

\emph{(iii), the past half.} On the generators ending on the edge, $u \le 0$, the future-directed boost is the reverse of the one on $u \ge 0$. $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{-}))$ is invariant under $\beta$, and on it the future-directed flow is $\gamma_{t} = \beta_{-t}$. Under $u \mapsto -u$ the kernel $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$ on $u, v < 0$ becomes $\tfrac{-I_{4}}{2\pi}(x - y - I_{4}0)^{-1}$ on $x, y > 0$, the complex conjugate of the kernel above, so on $\varphi_{w}(x) = x^{-1/2 + I_{4}w}$ its symbol is $m(-w) = (1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$; in the variable $x$ the flow $\gamma_{t}$ is $x \mapsto e^{-\kappa t}x$, whose one-particle generator acts on $\varphi_{w}$ as $+\kappa w$, so the symbol is $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ again. In strip form, for $u, v < 0$, $F(\lambda) = e^{-\lambda/2}\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(e^{-\lambda}u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$ continued to $\lambda + I_{4}\theta$ has denominator $e^{-I_{4}\theta}e^{-\lambda}u - v$, whose imaginary part $|u|e^{-\lambda}\sin\theta$ is positive on $(0, \pi)$ and negative on $(\pi, 2\pi)$, with no zero in the open strip and the weight factor $e^{-I_{4}\pi} = -1$ at $2\pi$: KMS at $+2\pi/\kappa$ for the future-directed boost; the past-directed boost on the same half gives $-2\pi/\kappa$. The check verifies the strip signs, a tabulated value, the reversed control and $m(w) + m(-w) = 1$.

\emph{(iii), the strip and what makes $2\pi$.} The same result in the form of the KMS condition: for $u, v > 0$ put $F(\lambda) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\,\beta_{\lambda/\kappa}(\psi(u))) = e^{\lambda/2}\tfrac{I_{4}}{2\pi}(e^{\lambda}u - v + I_{4}0)^{-1}$. As a function of $\lambda + I_{4}\theta$, $F$ is analytic wherever $e^{I_{4}\theta}e^{\lambda}u \ne v$; for $u, v > 0$ that fails only at $\theta \in 2\pi\Z$, so $F$ is analytic in $0 < \theta < 2\pi$. At $\theta \to 0^{+}$ the denominator approaches the real axis from above, the $+I_{4}0$ of $F$; at $\theta \to 2\pi^{-}$ from below, and the weight factor has become $e^{I_{4}\pi}e^{\lambda/2}$, so $F(\lambda + 2\pi I_{4}) = e^{\lambda/2}\tfrac{-I_{4}}{2\pi}(e^{\lambda}u - v - I_{4}0)^{-1} = \omega(\beta_{\lambda/\kappa}(\psi(u))\,\psi^{*}(v))$, the second ordering computed from (ii) (its kernel is $\delta(u - v) - A(u, v) = \tfrac{-I_{4}}{2\pi}(u - v - I_{4}0)^{-1}$). This is the two-point KMS identity at rapidity period $2\pi$; smearing with test functions supported in $u > 0$ makes it rigorous, and Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two} lifts it. Each ingredient is needed. (a) With the opposite energy sign the prescriptions swap, the boundary value at $\theta \to 0^{+}$ no longer matches, and the strip opens to $\theta < 0$: KMS at $-2\pi/\kappa$. (b) If one point lies on the other side of the edge, $u < 0 < v$, then $e^{I_{4}\pi}e^{\lambda}u = v$ at $e^{\lambda} = v/|u|$: a pole inside the strip at imaginary rapidity $\pi$, where the continued half-generator $e^{I_{4}\theta}\R_{+}$ reaches $\R_{-}$; the full-generator algebra is not KMS (the null vacuum on it is pure). (c) The weight is not a free ingredient: $e^{\lambda w_{0}}\psi(e^{\lambda}u)$ preserves $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)$ exactly when $\operatorname{Re}w_{0} = \tfrac12$, since $\delta(e^{\lambda}(u - v)) = e^{-\lambda}\delta(u - v)$; for that weight the factor at $2\pi$ is $e^{I_{4}\pi} = -1$, which carries the coefficient $I_{4}$ of one ordering to the coefficient $-I_{4}$ of the other, as the KMS identity requires. (An integer-weight bosonic field with its double-pole kernel gives the same period; the half weight is what the anticommutator forces here, not a separate reason for $2\pi$.) (d) No $\theta \in (0, 2\pi)$ is a return: $e^{I_{4}\theta}e^{\lambda}u - v$ is real only for $e^{I_{4}\theta}$ real, and at $\theta = \pi$ it is $-e^{\lambda}u - v \ne e^{\lambda}u - v$. The check verifies (a) to (d) exactly at Gaussian-rational points $e^{I_{4}\theta} = (1 - t^{2} + 2I_{4}t)/(1 + t^{2})$ of the unit circle: no zero for $u, v > 0$, the sign of the imaginary part equal to that of $t$, the zero at $\theta = \pi$ for $u < 0 < v$ with $e^{\lambda} = v/|u|$, that among the weights $\tfrac{k}{4}$ only $\tfrac12$ preserves the anticommutator ($\rho^{4w_{0}}\rho^{-2} = 1$ at $e^{\lambda/2} = \rho$) and that its factor $e^{I_{4}\pi}$ maps $I_{4}$ to $-I_{4}$, and the swapped prescription failing.
